title: Stress test of Within's public package, within-sdk 1.0.4: what fails, what a vendor can do about it, and what Within must fix
intro: Within sells analytics for AI tool calls. A company installs one npm package, `within-sdk`. It sits inside the company's MCP server, records every tool call, and sends a copy to Within. The package describes itself as "MCP analytics, workflow intelligence, and qualified opportunities".

This report lists what we found when we tried to break that package. Every finding has a plain-words explanation, then the technical detail, then **what a vendor can do today** with the package's own options, and **what Within must change**, shown by a patched copy that we tested.

Everything ran on our own machine against the published package, version 1.0.4, and a small stand-in for Within's server. We did not send load or attack traffic to Within's service, and we did not look at anything behind its login.

severity.name: High
severity.meaning: Can break or corrupt a vendor's own product, or sends a vendor's customer data to Within in a normal setup, in a way the docs do not say.

severity.name: Medium
severity.meaning: Breaks something the docs promise, or hurts in a less common setup, or only during an outage.

severity.name: Low
severity.meaning: A paper cut: confusing or untidy, but unlikely to hurt anyone.

summary: **In short.** {{V:n}} checks ran on Within's public package, version {{V:version}} ({{V:tally}}). We found {{V:count}} problems: {{V:high}} High, {{V:medium}} Medium and {{V:low}} Low.

**The most serious.** One long piece of unbroken text in a customer's request freezes the company's whole AI server for about {{V:stallSeconds}} seconds at 100,000 characters. The package's own size limit does not stop it. A vendor can avoid it today with its own redaction function, and Within can fix it by changing the order of two steps.

**Customer data.** The package sends what customers ask for, and what the company's tools answer, to Within by default. It hides only a short list of private details, and some only when they are the whole value.

**What a vendor can do.** {{V:mitigatedCount}} of the {{V:count}} problems have a fix that works today with the package's own options. {{V:patchedCount}} have a small change that Within could make, and we tested each one on a patched copy: {{V:patchSummary}}.

**What held up.** An outage at Within does not change or slow the company's own answers, a broken reply from Within does not hurt the company's tools, 40 customers at once do not mix their data, and the company's own instructions are left alone.

heldUp.text: When Within is down, the vendor's tool still returns its result.
The vendor's result, `structuredContent` and `_meta` are identical to an untracked server's, with Within up or down.
A broken (non-JSON) reply from Within does not hurt the vendor's tool.
40 customers at once with a slow Within overlap, and no customer's goal text is swapped with another's.
A vendor `identify` function that throws does not break the vendor's tool.
A vendor tool that already has an input called `context` keeps it: its handler gets the vendor's value. The package then sends that value to Within as the goal text.
A goal text of 2,000 characters is accepted.
The raw user id and name are not sent: a hashed subject goes out instead.
The vendor's server instructions are left unchanged.
A tool written with Zod 4 is tracked and called without a crash.
The README's install line and quickstart run on a fresh project.

notTested: Real Claude, ChatGPT or any host. The package has no sales or consent flow, so there is nothing for a model to decide, except whether it calls `get_more_tools` and writes a useful `context`.
Within's hosted service. The README says its ingestion applies an extra server-side redaction pass; we cannot see or test it.
The exporters for Datadog, OTLP, PostHog and Sentry, and the `publishCustomEvent` function.
How long Node's own network code waits before it gives up a stuck request (W-05). We watched for 15 seconds.
`apidocs.getwith.in`, named in the README, did not answer. Everything here is checked against the README and the code.
One machine, Node {{V:node}} on macOS, and the in-memory MCP transport. Not a deployed server, a container host or a real MCP client.
method: **Stand-in server.** Every request goes to a small local server on `127.0.0.1` or to a stubbed `fetch`. The log file goes to a throwaway home folder.

**Real package.** The checks use the published `within-sdk` {{V:version}} from npm, build an MCP server around it with the official MCP SDK ({{V:mcpSdk}}), and call its tools through an in-memory client.

**One process per check.** The package keeps one process-wide event queue, so a check that hangs Within would otherwise block every later check. The first full run, in one process, was invalid for exactly that reason, and W-05 is what that mistake revealed.

**Mitigations and patches.** Checks M1 to M8 try what a vendor can do with the package's own options. `stress/v104/patches.mjs` builds a patched copy with six small fixes (P1 to P6), each asserted to match exactly once, and runs the same checks on it.

findings.title: One long run of plain letters freezes the vendor's whole server for seconds
findings.plain: The package hides email addresses with a text pattern that gets much slower as the text gets longer, when the text has no spaces. It runs on every tool argument by default. We sent one argument of unbroken letters. At 10,000 letters the whole process stalled for {{R:C8.evidence.out[0].maxEventLoopStallMs}} ms, at 50,000 for {{R:C8.evidence.out[2].maxEventLoopStallMs}} ms and at 100,000 for {{R:C8.evidence.out[3].maxEventLoopStallMs}} ms. Ordinary words of the same length took {{R:C8.evidence.out[4].maxEventLoopStallMs}} ms. The vendor's own tool still answered in about {{R:C8.evidence.out[3].callMs}} ms, so the stall shows nowhere in the vendor's code. The pattern alone gives the same curve ({{R:C8b.evidence.rows[0].ms}}, {{R:C8b.evidence.rows[1].ms}}, {{R:C8b.evidence.rows[2].ms}} and {{R:C8b.evidence.rows[3].ms}} ms for 10,000, 25,000, 50,000 and 100,000 letters).
findings.why: While the process is stalled it cannot answer any customer. One customer pasting a long encoded string, or anyone trying to hurt the vendor, can stall the vendor's server for everyone else. The package runs inside the vendor's process, so its slowness is the vendor's slowness. The size limit of 10,000 bytes does not help, because it is applied after the pattern: with the limit set to 500 the stall was still {{R:M1.evidence.limit.maxEventLoopStallMs}} ms.
where: Lines 95 and 107: `truncateString(redactSensitiveString(value), …)` runs the pattern on the whole text first, then cuts it.
fix: Cut the text to the field limit before any pattern runs (patch P1).
Or replace the pattern with one that does not rescan: it should take time in proportion to the length. Add a test with a 100,000-character input.
findings.founder: One customer pasting a very long, unbroken piece of text can freeze the company's whole AI server for several seconds, for every other customer too. It happens in the normal setup, and the package's own size limit does not stop it.

mitigation.text: A redaction function that cuts every string to 2,000 characters brought the stall at 100,000 letters from {{R:M1.evidence.stock.maxEventLoopStallMs}} ms to {{R:M1.evidence.cut.maxEventLoopStallMs}} ms, because the vendor's function runs before the package's pattern. Setting the field limit alone does not help.

patch.text: With the cut moved before the pattern, the stall at 100,000 letters was {{P:C8.evidence.out[3].maxEventLoopStallMs}} ms.

findings.repro: cd stress/v104 && node checks.mjs C8 C8b

findings.title: Private details written inside a sentence are not hidden in the goal text, in arguments, in results or in error messages
findings.plain: The package hides a value only when it recognises the whole value, or recognises an email address or a bearer token inside text. Phone numbers, social security numbers and card numbers count only when they are the entire value. In text we sent, these went out as written: {{R:C2.evidence.survivors}} in the goal text; {{R:C5.evidence.survivors}} in a free-text argument; {{R:C3.evidence.survivors}} in an error message; and {{R:C4.evidence.survivors}} in the tool's result. Identity data is handled better: a user id and name are replaced by a hashed subject, but a phone number inside a free-text field of the identity data went out ({{R:C11.evidence.leaks}}), and so did one in the data of a conversion report ({{R:C13.evidence.leaks}}). The README says Within's own service applies a second redaction pass. We cannot see or test that.
findings.why: A customer who types a card number or a phone number into a question sends it to Within, unless the vendor has added its own redaction. A key written with hyphens (`sk-live-…`) goes through because the pattern wants an underscore.
where: `dist/modules/privacy.js` lines 140 to 158 and 176 to 183: the whole-value patterns (`PHONE_RE`, `SSN_RE`, `CREDIT_CARD_RE`, with `^` and `$`) and the underscore-only key pattern (`API_KEY_GLOBAL_RE`).
fix: Search for phone, social security and card numbers and for keys inside text, not only when they are the whole value.
Names and street addresses cannot be found by a pattern. Say so in the README, and make sending free text something the vendor turns on.
findings.founder: A customer who types a card number or a phone number into a question can have it sent to Within unhidden. The add-on hides only a short list of patterns, and only some of them inside a sentence.

mitigation.text: A vendor-written redaction function that masks digit runs, keys, web addresses and IP addresses left only {{R:M2.evidence.survivors}} unredacted in the arguments (names and street addresses cannot be matched by a pattern).

findings.repro: cd stress/v104 && node checks.mjs C2 C3 C4 C5 C11 C13

findings.title: Tool arguments and tool results go to Within by default, and the only off switch turns all reporting off
findings.plain: Every tool call is reported with its arguments and its result. In our run the query `acme corp` was in the event (seen: {{R:C1.evidence.hasArgs}}) and so was the result text (seen: {{R:C1.evidence.hasResult}}). The README says identity-like fields in parameters and responses are removed or redacted, which implies they are sent, but it lists no setting for leaving them out. Setting `enableTracing` to false stopped every report ({{R:Z2b.evidence.n}} events), and with it all the analytics. With the context and extra-tool switches off, {{R:Z2.evidence.n}} events still went out.
findings.why: The vendor's customers' questions and the vendor's own answers leave the vendor's server in a normal setup. The README mentions it only in the sentence about redaction.
where: `dist/modules/tracing.js` lines 208 to 259 build the tools/call event with `parameters: { request, extra }` (the request holds the arguments) and `event.response = result`. `tracingV2.js` lines 219 to 253 do the same.
fix: Make argument and result capture opt-in, and say in the README what leaves by default.
findings.founder: In a normal setup the add-on sends what customers ask for, and what the company's tools answer, to Within on every tool call. The setup page mentions this only in passing and lists no setting to stop it, short of turning off all reporting.

mitigation.text: A vendor can strip or mask what leaves with the `redactSensitiveInformation` option (see W-02). Turning off `enableTracing` stops everything.

findings.repro: cd stress/v104 && node checks.mjs C1 Z2 Z2b

findings.title: Argument names such as name, address, date of birth and IP address are not treated as private
findings.plain: The package hides an argument's value when its name contains one of 31 listed words, for example `email`, `phone`, `token`, `password`, `ssn` or `card`. We sent 18 differently named arguments. These went out with their values as written: {{R:C6.evidence.kept}}. The README says identity-like fields in parameters are removed or redacted.
findings.why: A vendor tool with an argument named `name`, `address` or `dob` sends that personal detail to Within, unless the vendor knows the list and adds its own words.
where: `dist/modules/privacy.js` lines 2 to 33 (the 31 words) and lines 130 to 136 (`isSecretKey` checks whether the lower-cased name contains one of them).
fix: Add `address`, `dob` and `birth` to the list, and treat `name`, `ip` and `customer` as secret when they are the whole name (patch P4).
findings.founder: The add-on hides a private detail only when the field is named with certain words, such as email or phone. A field called name, address or date of birth is sent as written.

mitigation.text: The documented `privacy.redactKeys` option fixed it: with name, address, dob, customer, ip and city listed, the names still sent as written were {{R:M3.evidence.kept}}.

patch.text: With the patch, the names still sent as written were {{P:C6.evidence.kept}}.

findings.title: When Within stops answering, later reports stay stuck behind the stuck ones, even after Within recovers
findings.plain: The package sends reports through one queue that runs at most five requests at a time, and a request has no time limit. We made the stand-in for Within accept requests and never answer. After {{R:A1c.evidence.hungPosts}} requests were stuck, reports for later tool calls waited behind them. Then the stand-in answered normally again. In the next 15 seconds, {{R:A1c.evidence.okPosts}} of the {{R:A1c.evidence.waiting}} waiting reports were sent. The vendor's own calls were not slowed: five calls took {{R:A1.evidence.times}} ms. We did not wait to find out when Node's own network code gives up a stuck request.
findings.why: A short outage at Within can silently remove the vendor's reports for later calls. The queue holds up to 10,000 reports and then drops the oldest. Nothing reaches the vendor's own code, and the only trace is the log file.
where: `dist/modules/eventQueue.js` line 17 (`concurrency = 5`), line 64 (`activeRequests++`) and line 211 (`postEvent`, which calls `fetch` at line 215 with no `signal` and no timeout).
Line 16: `maxQueueSize = 10000`, and line 34 drops the oldest event when the queue is full.
fix: Give every request an abort signal with a time limit of a few seconds, and count a timeout as a failed send that is retried (patch P2).
findings.founder: If Within's service stops answering for a while, the add-on can stop reporting anything to Within, and nobody is told. The company's own customers do not notice. We watched for 15 seconds after Within came back and saw no report sent.

mitigation.text: The package has a `fetch` option (declared in its type definitions, not in the README's table). Passing a `fetch` that adds a 1.5-second time limit let {{R:M5.evidence.got}} requests through in the 15 seconds after Within recovered, against {{R:A1c.evidence.okPosts}} without it.

patch.text: With a 5-second limit on every request inside the package, {{P:A1c.evidence.okPosts}} requests reached Within in the 15 seconds after it recovered.

findings.repro: cd stress/v104 && node checks.mjs A1 A1c

findings.title: A server that loads the package ignores the first request to shut down
findings.plain: When a hosting system wants a program to stop, it sends a signal called SIGTERM. A plain Node program exits at once ({{R:Z3.evidence.plain.ms}} ms in our test). Once the package is loaded, its own handler catches the first SIGTERM, waits for its queue to empty, and does not end the program. The server was still running after 12 seconds. A second SIGTERM, sent 3 seconds after the first, ended it after {{R:Z3.evidence.two.ms}} ms.
findings.why: Hosting systems commonly send SIGTERM first and stop the program by force later if it is still running. A server that needs a second signal slows every deploy and restart.
where: `dist/modules/eventQueue.js` lines 122 to 129: `process.once` for `SIGINT`, `SIGTERM` and `beforeExit`, each calling a `shutdown` that runs `eventQueue.destroy()` and never exits or re-sends the signal.
fix: After the queue is flushed, send the same signal again, or leave signal handling to the application (patch P3).
findings.founder: A company server that uses the add-on does not stop the first time the hosting system asks it to. It needs a second request, which slows every update of the company's server.

mitigation.text: A vendor's own handler (`process.on('SIGTERM', () => process.exit(0))`) ended the process on the first signal in {{R:M6.evidence.ms}} ms.

patch.text: With the patch, the first SIGTERM ended the process in {{P:Z3.evidence.one.ms}} ms.

findings.title: A vendor's redaction function is handed the API key and the address events go to, and changing them stops delivery silently
findings.plain: The vendor's `redactSensitiveInformation` function is applied to every string in the event except a short protected list. The list does not include the API key or the destination address. Our recording function was handed the API key ({{R:M8.evidence.sawKey}}) and the address ({{R:M8.evidence.sawUrl}}). A function that replaced digit runs, a natural way to hide phone numbers, rewrote the address from `http://127.0.0.1:PORT` to `http://N.N.N.N:N`. Every send then failed, and {{R:M8.evidence.delivered2}} events arrived, against {{R:M8.evidence.delivered1}} with a function that changes nothing. The failure shows only as lines in the log file.
findings.why: This is the option a vendor must use to fix W-01 to W-04. A vendor that masks numbers or web addresses can break reporting without any error in its own code. A function that writes strings to its own log would also write the API key.
where: `dist/modules/eventQueue.js` line 46 (the vendor's function is applied first) and `dist/modules/redaction.js` lines 6 to 16 (the protected list).
fix: Add `apiKey`, `ingestBaseUrl` and `vendorSlug` to the protected list (patch P6).
findings.founder: The recommended way to hide private details can silently stop all reporting, and it hands the company's secret key to the company's own hiding code. Nothing tells the company.

patch.text: With the three fields protected, the function was handed the API key: {{P:M8.evidence.sawKey}}, and the digit-replacing function delivered {{P:M8.evidence.delivered2}} events.

findings.title: Every tool call on the server is reported, and none can be left out
findings.plain: `track()` instruments the whole server. A tool registered after `track()` was reported too (reports for it: {{R:B7.evidence.reported}}). The package's type definitions declare 14 options. None leaves one tool out, and we found no such option in the code.
findings.why: A vendor with one internal or sensitive tool has no per-tool choice. The only ways out are to redact its strings or to turn tracing off for the whole server.
fix: Offer an option to leave named tools out, and say in the README that every tool is reported.
findings.founder: The add-on reports every tool the company's server has. The company cannot pick which ones.
findings.repro: cd stress/v104 && node checks.mjs B7 C1

findings.title: A missing or rejected key shows only in a log file in the home folder, and the file only grows
findings.plain: With no key and no exporter, `track()` does not complain: it writes one warning to `~/within-sdk.log`. With a wrong key (HTTP 401) the vendor's code gets no signal either: the log file holds {{R:A4.evidence.count}} lines about the failure. The log file is never rotated or capped (it only appends), and in our test one connection and one call added {{R:C12.evidence.bytes}} bytes. The log holds no vendor data in what we sent.
findings.why: A mistyped key means no analytics and no error. In a container the home folder is often not looked at.
where: `dist/modules/logging.js` lines 85 to 88 (`writeFileSync`, `appendFileSync`) and `dist/index.js` lines 36 to 38 (the missing-key warning).
fix: Fail loudly at start-up when no key and no exporter are set, or log to the console.
findings.founder: A mistyped key means Within gets nothing and nobody is told. The only trace is a growing file in a folder nobody reads.

mitigation.text: The `log` option takes a callback. With it, {{R:M4.evidence.lines}} lines went to the vendor's own code and {{R:M4.evidence.grew}} bytes were added to the file.

findings.repro: cd stress/v104 && node checks.mjs A4 A10 C12

findings.title: Every vendor tool gets a required "context" input, and the model sees one extra tool
findings.plain: After `track()`, each tool's input list gains a `context` text, marked as required, with a description that asks for 15 to 25 words. A call without it still worked in our test (required now: {{R:B5.evidence.required}}; the server did not reject the call). A tool with no inputs becomes a tool that takes only `context`. The model also sees a new tool, `get_more_tools`, whose description tells it to check for more tools "whenever your task might benefit from specialized capabilities".
findings.why: A client or model that follows the advertised list strictly has to write an explanation on every call. The tool list customers see is no longer the one the vendor wrote.
where: `dist/modules/context-parameters.js` lines 17 to 53 (adds `context` and pushes it into `required`) and `dist/modules/tracing.js` line 67 (adds `get_more_tools`).
fix: Do not mark `context` as required, since the server does not enforce it (patch P5).
findings.founder: The add-on changes the list of tools that customers' AI assistants see: it adds an explanation box to every tool and one extra tool.

mitigation.text: Two documented switches (`enableToolCallContext` and `enableReportMissing` set to false) left the tool list as the vendor wrote it.

patch.text: With the patch, the required inputs were {{P:B5.evidence.required}}.

findings.repro: cd stress/v104 && node checks.mjs B5 B5b Z1 Z2

findings.title: The docs' install line names a package that npm does not have
findings.plain: On 2026-11-22 the docs at getwith.in/docs told vendors to run `npm install @getwithin/sdk`. We asked npm for that package and it answered "not found" ({{R:F6.evidence.npmStatus}}). The package Within points to as public is `within-sdk`, which npm serves (version {{R:F6.evidence.publicVersion}}). The README of `within-sdk` names `apidocs.getwith.in`, which did not answer. We could not check which page the docs mean to be current.
findings.why: A vendor who follows the docs' install line gets an error and no package.
where: The docs page (getwith.in/docs, fetched {{R:F6.evidence.fetchedAt}}) and the npm registry (`registry.npmjs.org`).
fix: Change the docs' install line to `npm install within-sdk @modelcontextprotocol/sdk`.
findings.founder: The install instructions on Within's website name a software package that does not exist in the public package store. A company following them gets an error.
findings.repro: cd stress/v104 && node checks.mjs F6 F2
